linux_syscall_abi_table.red_zone_note: System V AMD64 ABI allows 128-byte red zone [rsp-128, rsp) in user space; POSIX signal delivery pushes ucontext/siginfo below rsp-128 unless SA_ONSTACK (sigaltstack) is active.

clobbered_by_kernel: x0 (return value); x1..x18 preserved by Linux kernel entry stub, though PCS treats x0..x18 as caller-saved across C calls
linux_syscall_abi_table.red_zone_note: AAPCS64 has 0-byte red zone in ELF user space; sp must be 16-byte aligned at every instruction that can fault or take an interrupt/signal.
RISC-V LP64D ABI has 0-byte red zone; sp (x2) must remain 16-byte aligned at all times.

platform_os_reachability.stable_boundary: Both Linux kernel syscall ABI (stable user-space contract) AND libc.so.6 / musl C ABI
platform_os_reachability.direct_syscall_usage: std uses libc + weak::syscall! for newer syscalls (getrandom, statx, clone3, futex); ecosystem crates (rustix linux_raw backend, linux-raw-sys) invoke raw syscall/svc/ecall via core::arch::asm!.

platform_os_reachability.stable_boundary: libSystem.B.dylib ONLY (raw Mach/BSD svc #0x80 numbers are explicitly unstable across macOS point releases)
platform_os_reachability.direct_syscall_usage: Forbidden by Apple ABI; all Rust std and rustix calls on macOS link against libSystem.B.dylib symbols.

platform_os_reachability.stable_boundary: Win32 DLL exports (kernel32.dll, advapi32.dll, ws2_32.dll, bcryptprimitives.dll, api-ms-win-core-*) and documented ntdll.dll exports (RtlNtStatusToDosError, NtWaitForKeyedEvent / WaitOnAddress); raw syscall numbers in ntdll change across Windows builds.
platform_os_reachability.direct_syscall_usage: Forbidden by Windows ABI; all OS calls go through PE32+ import tables (.idata) into Win32/ntdll DLLs.

environment_assumption_ledger_entries.summary: OS loader (ld-linux / dyld / ntdll LdrInitializeThunk) maps PT_LOAD / __TEXT,__DATA / PE sections with declared permissions, zeroes .bss, applies dynamic relocations, and initializes TLS (fs:0 / tpidr_el0 / tp / gs:[0x58]) before jumping to _start / mainCRTStartup.

Every OS syscall or dynamic library call preserves callee-saved registers, caller stack frames outside passed mutable buffers, and read-only segments, modifying only the return register(s) and explicitly passed out-pointer memory ranges.

Heap allocations returned by malloc/posix_memalign/realloc (unix.rs) or HeapAlloc/HeapReAlloc (windows.rs) return fresh, properly aligned, non-overlapping address ranges disjoint from all live stack frames, globals, and previously allocated live heap blocks.

environment_assumption_ledger_entries.category: Stack Guard Page & Stack Probe Contract
environment_assumption_ledger_entries.summary: The OS maintains at least one unmapped guard page below each thread stack; compiler-emitted stack probes (__rust_probestack / inline page-touch loop) touch each 4 KiB page sequentially so frames > 4 KiB cannot skip the guard page.

Compiled code never writes below sp (except within the 128-byte x86-64 red zone on SysV leaf functions when red-zone is enabled), keeps sp 16-byte aligned at all potentially faulting or interruptible instructions on AArch64/RISC-V/Windows, and assumes signal handlers execute on sigaltstack (SA_ONSTACK, configured by std::sys::pal::unix::stack_overflow) or respect the active stack pointer and red zone.
